Молодой, но талантливый физик Федя соору: A young but talented physicist Fedya built a thermal water-lifting machine at his dacha. Its design and principle of operation are simple. A cylindrical closed pipe is buried halfway into the ground. Inside the pipe is a massive tightly fitted piston that can move along the pipe; to limit its movement inside the pipe, Fedya placed small stops. At ground level, a tube with a valve leads to the middle of the pipe, through which water can enter the pipe. At the top of the pipe, there is a tube for draining water. The working fluid of the machine is air. To reduce the temperature to which the air must be heated, a cylindrical heater tank with an electric heater inside is connected to the pipe.
Описание работы машины начнем с начально: Let's start describing the machine's operation from the initial state {#0}: the piston is at the bottom, water fills half of the pipe (up to ground level), the valve is closed, the heater is on, and the piston begins to rise, lifting the water.
После того, как поршень прошел половину: After the piston has passed half the pipe length (Fig. {0}), water begins to spill out from the top. When the piston reaches the top point, all the water spills out; after that, the heater turns off and the piston starts to descend. Once it goes below ground level, Fedya opens the valve, and the incoming water helps the piston descend to the lower position (Fig. {1}). Then the process repeats.
